Class SinglesCubeIdx

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.util.SinglesCubeIdx
public final class SinglesCubeIdx extends Object
Geometry and slot indexing shared by Singles Stack rendering, collision, ray targeting, and support.

A block contains a 4 x 4 x 4 grid indexed from the bottom layer upward and row by row within each layer. Each cell is supported by the cell directly below it. At a block boundary, callers supply the lower block's top-layer occupancy as the supporting seam. Support follows visual columns rather than storage indexes, so adjacent blocks remain aligned even when rotated differently.

  • Method Details

    • freshBlockSupports

      public static boolean freshBlockSupports(int index, boolean[] seamBelow)
      Whether a prospective Singles Stack could support an item at index. Since all of its slots are still empty, only the bottom layer can be supported. It is grounded when there is no Singles Stack below; otherwise its visual column must be occupied in seamBelow. New blocks are unrotated, so index is already in the visual frame.

    • isGrounded

      public static boolean isGrounded(int index, SlotAccess handler, int blockRotation, boolean[] seamBelow)
      Whether a cell has support. Cells above the bottom consult the cell beneath them in the same storage column. The bottom layer consults seamBelow, the top-layer occupancy of the Singles Stack underneath. A null seam means there is no Singles Stack below, so the bottom layer is grounded.

    • isGroundedIn

      public static boolean isGroundedIn(boolean[] occupancy, int index, int blockRotation, boolean[] seamBelow)
      Applies isGrounded(int, SlotAccess, int, boolean[]) to an occupancy snapshot rather than live slots, so a proposed placement can be validated without mutating inventory.

    • seamSupports

      public static boolean seamSupports(int index, int blockRotation, boolean[] seamBelow)
      Whether the top layer beneath a block occupies the visual column containing index.

    • storageColumnFromVisual

      public static int storageColumnFromVisual(int visualColumn, int blockRotation)
      The storage column a visual column occupies under a block rotation, the inverse of visualColumnFromStorage(int, int). The four rotations form a cycle, so the inverse of r is its normalized inverse.

    • topLayerOccupancy

      public static boolean[] topLayerOccupancy(SlotAccess handler, int blockRotation)
      Returns top-layer occupancy in visual columns, the coordinate system shared across a block boundary even when adjacent blocks have different rotations.

    • traceAllPositions

      public static int traceAllPositions(ViewRay ray, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos blockPos)
      Finds the deposit target for a Singles Stack that does not yet exist and therefore has no occupied slots. Placement uses this to validate the initial deposit and its resulting collision shape before adding the block to the world. New blocks are unrotated.

    • traceAllPositions

      public static int traceAllPositions(ViewRay ray, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos blockPos, @Nullable SlotAccess handler, int blockRotation)
      Finds the slot a deposit targets: the last empty slot along the view ray before the first occupied one, or the farthest intersected slot if the ray meets no occupied item. A null handler describes a prospective, entirely empty block.

    • traceCubes

      public static int traceCubes(ViewRay ray, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos blockPos, SinglesStackBE be)
      Returns the nearest occupied cell intersected by the view ray, or -1 on a miss.

    • visualColumnFromStorage

      public static int visualColumnFromStorage(int storageColumn, int blockRotation)
      The visual column a storage column occupies under a block rotation. Rotation permutes x and z but never y, so columns always map to columns and only their horizontal identity moves.

    • rotateXYZ

      public static int[] rotateXYZ(int x, int y, int z, int rotation)
      The visual position of a stored cell under a block rotation. A rotation is that many quarter turns counterclockwise seen from above, matching the direction of per-item rotation.
